newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heat oil ends up on firm demand, crude dips.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heat oil ends up on firm demand, crude dips.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil futures held the gains made early Tuesday to settle more than 1.00 cent up on the day, aided by cold weather in the Northeast, which helped reverse the usual seasonal weakness.
April heating oil futures gained 1.10 cents to settle at 56.83 cents a gallon, not far off its session peak at 57.10 cents.
Crude oil futures dipped slightly ahead of the close on expectations of a bearish American Petroleum Institute inventory report, traders said. The May contract shed seven cents to finish at $20.99.
April gasoline futures finished up 0.01 cent at 66.52 cents a gallon in what traders described as "a nothing day," with the contract holding to an 80-point range.
However, both April heating oil and gasoline dipped during overnight Access trading in reaction to the weekly API data, while the May crude oil futures firmed modestly.
U.S. crude oil stocks fell 2.217 million barrels in the latest reporting week, according to the API, though that figure includes a 3.4 million barrel draw on the West Coast.
Gasoline stocks increased by 1.116 million barrels despite calls by most market watchers for a draw. Total U.S. stocks remain about 7.8 million barrels below year-ago levels.
The API report also showed a larger-than-expected jump in refinery utilization of 1.7 percentage points to put output at 92.7 percent of capacity.
Distillate inventories, which include home heating oil and diesel fuel stocks, fell 1.344 million barrels -- in line with traders expectations.
-- Matt Daily, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
